Sure. I think that both fear and awareness are things we have evolved in order to keep us alive, but in today's world it's not as useful as it was in a "kill or be killed" type on environment. For example, perhaps an early ancestor of yours was walking down a path at night and heard a rustle in the brush. He took off running, because he was afraid. The rustle could have been a predator, or maybe it was just the wind. Either way he survived and got to pass on his genes to the next generation.

If he decided to run every time the wind blew, however, he would quickly exhaust his energy and die. Perhaps it was daytime and he judged that there was no imminent threat. So awareness plays a key part, and both work mutually with each other.

We don't live in that world, but yet we carry on those genes. Fear is still useful from a survival point of view, but can quickly exhaust you if you don't try and assess the real threat.
